cards.title: What the coordination tier covers
cards.what_we_see: 4121 critical-term event revisions in 959 articles (diff status {'ok': 4121}); 3206 account events used after excluding {'anon': 902, 'bot': 51} (anonymous, hidden-user, bot, deleted). One run-wide pseudonymous ID per account.
cards.so_what: All tests below share these events; topic and comparison articles are tested separately.
cards.caveat: Lead events come from mass2's grid (exact events only) and the ratchet key articles; edits outside those events are invisible here. IP and temporary accounts are excluded from account-level tests.

cards.title: (a) Bloc detection: topic articles, any events
cards.what_we_see: topic articles, any events: 14 account pairs share articles above the rewiring null (p<0.01, >=3 shared); null worlds give 1.93 such pairs on average (95th 5.0). 2 candidate groups of 3+ (null worlds: 0.3 on average, 95th 1.0); 1 pass the bloc test. Bloc A (4 accounts) [medium]: 23 articles (top: Israel, Gaza war, Hamas, Israeli bombing of the Gaza Strip); 45 insertions / 23 removals; articles touched by 3+ members 3 vs null 0.236 (95th 1.0, p=0.001); 60-min cross-article co-activity 0 vs 0.12 (p=1.000, article-shuffle p=1.000); median same-article gap 333.87 h, events with another member within 10 min 0.0; 4 significant triads; null worlds with a bloc this large and dense: 0.0; active 2021-04-16 to 2025-11-15

null_model.bloc: articles with 3+ members vs rewiring; selection-aware share of null worlds; synchrony vs account day-shift (1-7 d) and time shuffle within article

cards.so_what: A bloc is a set of accounts whose overlap in critical-term articles is not explained by how active each account is and how popular each article is.
cards.caveat: Shared interest (WikiProject members, watchlists, talk-page RfCs) also produces overlap beyond a degree-preserving null; synchrony and direction help separate it but do not prove coordination.

cards.title: (b) Synchrony: topic account pairs acting on different articles within 10 minutes
cards.what_we_see: 0 pairs (0 accounts) acted on 3+ distinct article pairs within 10 min of each other more often than the account day-shift null (p<0.01); 0 also beat the within-article time-shuffle null. Null worlds give 0.05 pairs on average (95th 0.0).

null_model.null: each account's timeline shifted by a random 1-7 days (either sign), 1000 draws; secondary: timestamps permuted within article

cards.so_what: Pairs that repeatedly move together across different articles within minutes are the classic canvassing / sockpuppet signature, if they are more than the null expects.
cards.caveat: Both accounts may react to the same external trigger (news, an RfC closing, a noticeboard thread).

null_model.edge: p<0.01 and observed>=3 on 30-min cross-article co-activity (account day-shift) or shared articles (rewiring)

cards.so_what: The page's network graph; edges carry direction agreement, so insert-blocs and remove-blocs are visible.
cards.caveat: Edges are tested one by one at p<0.01; compare the edge count with the chance expectation, not with zero.

cards.title: (c) Copy-paste sweeps: topic articles
cards.what_we_see: 0 near-identical inserted sentences (5-word shingle Jaccard >= 0.7) appear in 5+ articles.

null_model.null: same number of insertion times drawn from all term insertions in the group, 1000 draws; statistic: shortest span covering 5 distinct articles

cards.so_what: A sweep is the same wording placed into many articles; a short span and few accounts point to a campaign, a long span and many accounts to a shared standard phrase.
cards.caveat: Standard wording (WikiProject templates, a source's stock phrase) also repeats; the temporal null separates bursts from slow diffusion, not intent.

cards.title: (c) Nakba wording on Palestinian village pages
cards.what_we_see: 25 inserted Nakba / expulsion sentences on 17 village pages by 15 registered accounts. Sweeps (5+ village articles, same wording): 0.
cards.so_what: Flags whether the village-page Nakba wording arrived as one sweep or piecemeal.
cards.caveat: Village articles share a WikiProject structure (Khalidi / Morris sourcing), so similar wording is expected; only a short-span, few-account cluster suggests a sweep.

cards.title: (e) Do detected blocs line up with the documented canvassing windows and sanctions?
cards.what_we_see: Sets tested: 3 (insert-direction blocs 1, remove-direction 0, any-direction blocs and communities 2). 0 show window concentration or a post-sanction drop beyond matched random sets (p<0.01). Bloc A (4 accounts) [topic/any]: email_canvassing: 41% of events in window [CI 17%-74%] vs matched sets 18% [0%-44%], own-span 0.149, others 0.169, p_high 0.042; tfp_discord: 21% of events in window [CI 12%-44%] vs matched sets 23% [4%-49%], own-span 0.226, others 0.253, p_high 0.5385. after 2024-12-09: drop ratio 0.392 [CI 0.028-1.104] vs matched 1.917, p_drop 0.1968; after 2025-04-25: drop ratio 0.597 [CI 0.118-0.887] vs matched 0.835, p_drop 0.5435 | topic network community 1 (4 accounts) [topic/any]: email_canvassing: 41% of events in window [CI 17%-74%] vs matched sets 18% [0%-40%], own-span 0.149, others 0.169, p_high 0.02; tfp_discord: 21% of events in window [CI 12%-44%] vs matched sets 23% [2%-47%], own-span 0.226, others 0.253, p_high 0.5325. after 2024-12-09: drop ratio 0.392 [CI 0.028-1.104] vs matched 2.238, p_drop 0.1818; after 2025-04-25: drop ratio 0.597 [CI 0.118-0.887] vs matched 0.877, p_drop 0.5335 | Bloc B (4 accounts) [topic/insert]: email_canvassing: 34% of events in window [CI 24%-42%] vs matched sets 15% [0%-38%], own-span 0.115, others 0.154, p_high 0.0509; tfp_discord: 29% of events in window [CI 12%-37%] vs matched sets 24% [3%-44%], own-span 0.231, others 0.246, p_high 0.3157. after 2024-12-09: drop ratio 0.224 [CI 0.032-1.8] vs matched 2.052, p_drop 0.0539; after 2025-04-25: drop ratio 0.218 [CI 0.02-1.072] vs matched 0.703, p_drop 0.3636

null_model.window_share: matched random account sets (member-by-member on event count), 1,000 draws; CI = bootstrap over members
null_model.post_sanction_drop: 365 d after vs before each date, relative to all other accounts; same matched-set null

cards.title: (d) Account profiles of the blocs (aggregate)
cards.what_we_see: Bloc A (4 accounts) topic/any: median age 1071.0 d (base 1298.5), editcount<500 0.0 (base 0.222), blocked now 0.25 (base 0.151, random-set 95th 0.5) | Bloc B (4 accounts) topic/insert: median age 2204.0 d (base 1322.0), editcount<500 0.0 (base 0.217), blocked now 0.25 (base 0.163, random-set 95th 0.5)

null_model.null: 1,000 random account sets of the same size from accounts with 2+ articles in the same scope; base rate = all accounts in scope

cards.so_what: Young, low-editcount or since-blocked blocs are the sockpuppet profile; veteran blocs look like WikiProject regulars.
cards.caveat: Block status is as of collection, not as of the edit.
